about: I started building for the web while studying computer engineering in Damascus, and grew into full-stack work for agencies, SaaS companies and product teams across the USA, the Gulf and Europe. Today I lead development on Dalelo, work as a full-stack engineer at ShrubHub, and run Builderization, my own software studio.

I care about the parts users never see as much as the parts they do: clean data models, secure APIs, fast pages, sensible deployments and backups. I design in Figma when a product needs it, and I build right-to-left Arabic interfaces as comfortably as English ones.

AI coding agents (Claude Code) are part of my daily workflow — always driven by written specs, tests and review gates, and with every change reviewed and owned by me. It lets a small team ship products such as Marhaba Syria and Ahaloop without lowering the bar.

case_study.overview: Smart Lab is a desktop application that medical laboratories use to run their day: registering patients and visits, printing barcoded tubes, receiving results from analyzers, validating and printing reports, and tracking payments, insurance, expenses and stock. It works in Arabic, English and Turkish.
case_study.problem: The previous version had grown screen by screen. Reception needed many clicks to register a visit and find earlier results, settings were scattered, and analyzer results were typed in by hand. The company needed a faster, consistent interface and a codebase that could keep growing.
case_study.role: I owned the redesign end to end: I mapped the lab workflow with the team, designed the new interface in Figma (reception, results entry, work tables, control panel, printed A4 reports) and led the rebuild of the Vue frontend and the backend services behind it.
responsibilities: Workflow mapping and UX design with lab staff
Design system and all key screens in Figma, RTL first
Vue 2 + Vuetify architecture: routing, Vuex stores, vue-i18n (ar/en/tr)
Node.js/Express + Sequelize API for patients, visits, tests, accounting and settings
Analyzer integration and Windows packaging with Electron
features: Reception: search by name, code or barcode; visit history; one-screen registration
Results entry with reference ranges by sex and age, notes and validation
Work tables per lab section showing ready and pending tests
Analyzer connections (e.g. Mindray, Immulite) configured from the control panel
Invoices, receipts, partial payments, insurance companies and associations
Expenses, daily accounts, statistics dashboard and inventory
Per-page permissions (view, add, edit, delete) for each role
Printed A4 reports; results shared as PDF or via WhatsApp
Scheduled compressed database backups with restore
case_study.architecture:
Electron shell → Vue 2 SPA (Vuetify · Vuex · vue-i18n)
      ↓ HTTP on localhost / LAN
Node.js + Express API (~60 controllers, Sequelize models)
      ↓
MySQL on the lab PC or a LAN server
Analyzers → ASTM / vendor parsers → results tables

challenges.challenge: Every analyzer model sends results in its own format.
challenges.solution: Per-device parsers (ASTM and vendor formats) behind one interface, configured from the control panel, so a new analyzer is added without touching the results screens.

challenges.challenge: Reception must stay fast during the morning rush, with Arabic text mixed with Latin test names.
challenges.solution: A single reception screen — patient list, search and visit form side by side — keyboard friendly, RTL first, with bilingual test names.

challenges.challenge: Labs run on local PCs where losing data is not an option.
challenges.solution: Local MySQL with scheduled compressed backups and a restore tool in the control panel.

challenges.challenge: Shipping a web stack as a desktop product.
challenges.solution: The Vue app and the Node backend are packaged together with Electron into a Windows installer.

case_study.notes: Smart Lab is owned by the client; screens shown are design files and screenshots without patient data. Source code is private.

projects.seo_title: Dalelo classifieds marketplace — lead developer case study | Ahmad Bayrakdar
projects.seo_description: Lead developer on Dalelo: mobile-app API, security hardening, structured locations, Google Maps cost controls and a full RTL redesign of a large classifieds marketplace.

cover.alt: Dalelo homepage with hero carousel and listing search card

gallery.alt: Dalelo homepage with hero carousel and listing search card

case_study.overview: Dalelo (دليلو) is an Arabic-first classifieds marketplace for Syria and the region, with tens of thousands of real-estate and vehicle listings plus services, places and hotels. It runs on the web and in native mobile apps, in Arabic, English and Turkish, with prices shown in 19 currencies.
case_study.problem: The platform is built on Flynax, a commercial PHP classifieds engine, and has been extended over the years by several developers. It needed a lead developer to keep production stable while adding the features the mobile apps depend on, closing security gaps, controlling Google Maps costs and moving the site to a new design.
case_study.role: Lead developer in a small team (another developer and a designer). I work across the PHP backend, the database, the admin panel and the front end; changes go to a QA server first, then to production.
responsibilities: Plan and ship platform features for web, admin and the mobile apps
Security review and fixes across admin, API and payments
Performance and cost controls for maps and geocoding
Implement the new design across every page, in light and dark
features: Mobile API: home data with featured listings, category tree, search and search-on-map, reels feeds, saved-search alerts, account and media endpoints
Structured Areas: areas seeded from existing listings; in-area results first, then nearby by distance; typo-tolerant autocomplete
Listing lifecycle: old-listing badges with self-service renewal, sold/rented filters, required photos and price
Hotels directory with map-picked locations and photo galleries
Composed share images (photos, price, location) for social link previews
Admin: listing review queue, agency and governorate statistics, API blacklist
Redesign: header, search card, listing and detail pages, directories, account pages, dark mode
case_study.architecture:
Web browsers · iOS & Android apps
      ↓ HTTPS
PHP (Flynax core + custom plugins, Smarty templates)
  ├─ API plugin: token auth · rate limits · blacklist → mobile apps
  └─ Admin panel: review, statistics, settings
      ↓
MySQL · media storage · Google Maps Platform (cached, rate-limited)

challenges.challenge: A security review found injectable queries, insecure direct object references and missing authorization in older admin and API code.
challenges.solution: Fixed each finding at the source: escaped and parameterised queries, ownership checks on listing and media edits, CSRF origin checks in the admin panel, server-side payment amounts, and credential fields stripped from public account APIs.

challenges.challenge: Map and geocoding calls were a growing cost and a target for bots.
challenges.solution: Per-bucket rate limits, a permanent blacklist for repeat offenders, cached Static Maps and Place Details, Places session tokens and throttled reverse geocoding.

challenges.challenge: Free-text locations made search by area unreliable.
challenges.solution: A structured Areas model built in phases: data clean-up, an areas table seeded from existing listings, local resolution before calling Google, and an admin Areas page.

challenges.challenge: Redesigning a live right-to-left site without breaking it.
challenges.solution: Eight staged releases on a QA server, each with light and dark regression passes, followed by English and Turkish passes.

results: Security findings closed across admin, API and payment flows.
New design live across the site in light and dark modes.
case_study.notes: Dalelo is built on the licensed Flynax platform; this case study covers custom work only. Visual design by the Dalelo design team.

case_study.overview: Builderization is my software studio. The site sells custom websites, apps, business systems, design work and small fixes to businesses, agencies (white-label) and companies, and turns visitors into WhatsApp conversations or project briefs.
case_study.problem: The site had to speak to three audiences in two languages and look nothing like a template, while staying fast and cheap to run on a small server that also hosts other services.
case_study.role: Everything: positioning, copy direction, the design system and illustrations, front end, lead API, infrastructure and deployment.
features: Service pages with a multi-select project-brief form that pre-selects the service
WhatsApp-first contact channels in the header, footer, pages and a floating button
"Ray Kira" flat illustration system: colour bands, hard offset shadows, 23 SVG characters
Motion layer (GSAP + ScrollTrigger) driven by data attributes, off for reduced motion
Work showcase, agency and enterprise pages, blog and legal pages
Client demo apps (e.g. a kiosk prize wheel) built and shipped by the same pipeline, including an Android APK built in CI
case_study.architecture:
Browser → nginx (TLS) on an Ubuntu VPS
  ├─ builderization-web.service — TanStack Start SSR (Node)
  ├─ site-api.service — lead API
  └─ static demo apps
git push main → GitLab CI build → rsync → systemctl restart

challenges.challenge: Two languages and two text directions without duplicated pages.
challenges.solution: One route tree; every visible string is an {en, ar} pair rendered through a t() helper, with direction-aware layout.

challenges.challenge: Rich illustration and motion without hurting speed or accessibility.
challenges.solution: Characters are inline SVG with named parts animated after hydration; prefers-reduced-motion switches motion off.
Each service is its own systemd unit behind nginx; CI deploys with rsync so a release never touches the others.

case_study.overview: Ahaloop makes short vertical videos about why everyday things exist. The whole chain — idea, research, script, storyboard, illustration, voice, music, edit, review and publishing — runs as a pipeline, with a human approving through Telegram.
case_study.problem: Making short videos consistently is slow, and generic AI video tools give repetitive, low-quality output. The goal was a pipeline that keeps quality high with checks at every stage and costs almost nothing to run.
case_study.role: Designed and built the system: the studio CLI, Claude Code skills, quality gates, rendering kits and the VPS publishing gateway.
features: Idea research with a novelty gate against past recipes
Script, storyboard and vector scenes animated by element id
Local text-to-speech and music composed as JSON, rendered locally
Automated review of every asset; failures loop back
Cadence planner and a local control panel
Publishing queue with platform uploaders and an OAuth connect site
case_study.architecture:
Task Scheduler → claude -p /produce-next (Claude Code skills)
  → studio CLI: research · script · storyboard · draw · voice · music · compose · review
  → render (HyperFrames / Blender) → upload to the VPS gateway
VPS: FastAPI queue · YouTube / TikTok / Instagram / Facebook uploaders · OAuth connect · Telegram bot

challenges.challenge: LLM output drifts and repeats itself.
challenges.solution: A novelty gate compares each idea with past recipes, and a review gate scores every asset before it moves on.

challenges.challenge: Platform APIs want a stable IP and long-lived tokens.
challenges.solution: Uploads run only from the VPS gateway, which keeps OAuth tokens server-side and publishes from a schedule queue.
Free stock sources, local TTS and music synthesis, and scenes drawn as vectors in code.

case_study.overview: Marhaba Syria is a classifieds marketplace designed for Syria first — property, cars, jobs and services — in Arabic and English.
case_study.problem: Local classifieds are noisy and hard to trust: duplicate ads, scam messages, little moderation and weak search. The goal is a marketplace with structured listings, real moderation and safe messaging.
case_study.role: I defined the product (23 planning documents), the architecture and the data model, and built the platform. I use AI coding agents (Claude Code) heavily on this codebase, working from written specs and acceptance criteria; I review and own every change.
features: Structured listing forms per category from a shared taxonomy
Typesense search, saved searches and favourites
Listing lifecycle: renew, mark sold, auto-expire
Messaging that flags shared phone numbers and links
Moderation scoring and a review queue
OTP sign-in for users, MFA for staff
Wallet and ledger with payment adapters (sandbox)
case_study.architecture:
apps/web (Next.js, next-intl) · apps/admin (Next.js, MFA) · apps/worker (BullMQ)
packages: auth · db (Drizzle) · search · payments · trust · ui · i18n · observability
PostgreSQL 16 (RLS) · Redis · Typesense · Cloudflare R2 · GitLab CI

challenges.challenge: Keeping the marketplace safe without a large moderation team.
challenges.solution: A trust package with moderation scoring, a review queue and message scanning for contact details shared too early.

challenges.challenge: Three apps that must stay consistent.
challenges.solution: Shared packages for db, auth, i18n and UI in a Turborepo, with one Drizzle schema and forward-only migrations.

challenges.challenge: Defence in depth for user data.
challenges.solution: PostgreSQL row-level security, atomic OTP verification and strict body limits on webhooks.

case_study.notes: In active development; not publicly launched yet.
